details: CONFIRMED by a probe. A .git file only says the git folder is elsewhere; linked worktrees, submodules and --separate-git-dir all
use it. And dirname(--git-common-dir) is the main checkout only when the common dir is <main>/.git. The exact test is
`rev-parse --git-dir` != `rev-parse --git-common-dir` (true only for a linked worktree), and the main checkout is the first
"worktree <path>" line of `git worktree list --porcelain`. Size: 15 agent minutes with the two tests.
evidence: python3 -I probe.py (lib on sys.path), after building the repos in the scratchpad:
failing_case: A main checkout whose .git is a file but which is not a linked worktree:
- a submodule super/mods/sub (.git = "gitdir: ../../.git/modules/mods/sub"): main_checkout() returns super/.git/modules/mods,
so `relay setup super/mods/sub` refuses: "Run `relay setup <super>/.git/modules/mods` on the main checkout".
- `git init --separate-git-dir=$S/sep.git sepwork`: main_checkout(sepwork) returns $S (the parent of sep.git), so setup refuses
and names an unrelated folder.
Should: both are their own main checkout; main_checkout() returns None and setup runs.
fix_hint: In main_checkout(): return None unless git-dir and git-common-dir (both --path-format=absolute) differ; then take the path of
the first "worktree " line of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
pass_cases: 1. git init --separate-git-dir=<tmp>/sep.git <tmp>/sepwork; main_checkout(<tmp>/sepwork) is None; setup(<tmp>/sepwork, flow="none",
product=False, apply_global=False) returns d["name"] == "sepwork".
2. A submodule <tmp>/super/mods/sub added with git submodule add: main_checkout() is None.
3. A linked worktree <tmp>/somewt of <tmp>/mainproj: main_checkout() == realpath(<tmp>/mainproj) (the existing test keeps passing).
4. A plain main checkout (.git folder) and a folder outside git: main_checkout() is None.
reason: tests/test_setup.py test_main_checkout_is_exact_for_each_kind_of_checkout covers worktree, main, loose, sepwork, submodule; passes, fails at 901966a.
findings.summary: main_checkout() takes any .git file for a linked worktree: a submodule or a --separate-git-dir checkout is refused with a wrong path

details: CONFIRMED by reading: migrate() (lib/relay_setup.py 779-797) runs the shutil.move loop and the bin/kit copy before it calls
setup(root, relay_dir=False, ...), and the new refusal sits at the top of setup(). The change put the check in the callee
but migrate writes first. Size: 10 agent minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_setup.py:783-795  if apply and items: ... shutil.move(src, dst) ... shutil.copy2(... "kit-shim" ...)
lib/relay_setup.py:634-636  main = main_checkout(root); if main: raise ValueError(...)
failing_case: A linked worktree of a project with old agents/skills/hooks (migration_plan lists items); run `relay migrate <worktree> --apply`.
Now: migrate() moves each item into .claude/relay-migration/ and writes bin/kit, then calls setup(), which raises "is a linked
git worktree"; the CLI prints the refusal and exits 1 with the files already moved and settings.json still calling the moved
hooks. Should: refuse before anything is moved; the worktree is unchanged.
fix_hint: Move the refusal into one helper (refuse_linked_worktree(root)) and call it first in both migrate() and setup().
pass_cases: 1. Linked worktree with an old .claude/agents/x.md that migration_plan lists; migrate(wt, apply=True, flow="none", product=False,
apply_global=False) raises ValueError naming the main checkout; .claude/agents/x.md is still there; no .claude/relay-migration
and no bin/kit were created.
2. The same with apply=False: raises the same ValueError, nothing written.
3. migrate(main_checkout, apply=True, ...) still moves the items and runs setup (existing migrate tests keep passing).
reason: tests/test_setup.py test_migrate_apply_in_a_linked_worktree_completes: migration completes, no half state; passes, fails at 901966a.
findings.summary: relay migrate --apply in a linked worktree moves the old files aside and writes bin/kit, then setup refuses: a half-migrated tree

details: CONFIRMED by reading: cmd_migrate_all loops over known_projects() with no try around migrate(); without --primary it already
skips every folder with a .git folder, so after this change it can only migrate folders outside git, and a worktree root aborts
the whole run. A caller of setup() not updated. Today only [relay] is registered, so it is reachable but not live.
evidence: bin/relay:444  if not primary and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(root, ".git")):  ... "primary checkout: skipped"
bin/relay:450  d, items, moved, ... = relay_setup.migrate(root, apply=bool(apply), apply_global=False)
bin/relay:881  except (relay_rules.Fail, FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as exc: print ...; return 1
failing_case: projects.toml lists project A at a linked worktree and project B after it. `relay migrate --all` (without --primary, which skips
every main checkout) copies A's kit drafts, then relay_setup.migrate(A) raises the new ValueError out of the loop; main() prints
"relay migrate: ... is a linked git worktree ..." and exits 1; B is never visited. Should: print a skip line for A (with the
command to run) and go on to B.
fix_hint: In cmd_migrate_all, check relay_setup.main_checkout(root) beside the primary check and print "linked worktree of <main>:
pass_cases: 1. RELAY_PROJECTS with A (a linked worktree's CLAUDE.local.md) then B (a folder without .git): cmd_migrate_all([]) prints a
"linked worktree: skipped" line for A, migrates B, and returns 0.
2. A registry with only a main checkout and no --primary: still prints "primary checkout: skipped" (unchanged).
3. With --primary on a main checkout: still migrates it.
reason: tests/test_setup.py test_migrate_all_with_a_worktree_registered_completes_and_reaches_later_projects: exit 0 and the later project reached; passes, fails at 901966a.
findings.summary: relay migrate --all stops at the first registered project whose folder is a linked worktree; later projects are not migrated

details: CONFIRMED by reading docs/setup.md 16, 81, 127-130 against the new backup(). The rollback promise is what a person reads to undo
evidence: docs/setup.md:16  `Bash(kit:*)` allowed; a backup beside it;
docs/setup.md:81  Revert: `mv .claude/relay-migration/<file> <back>`; the settings backup is beside the file.
failing_case: A person rolls back a project setup by docs/setup.md: "Revert: ... the settings backup is beside the file" (line 81; also line
16 "a backup beside it" and the rollback list at 127-130). After this change .claude/settings.json in a git project has no .bak
beside it: the copy is in <git dir>/relay-backup/.claude__settings.json.<stamp>.bak, or none when git holds the file unchanged
(restore with git). The person finds no backup. Also the worktree refusal is not in the docs.
fix_hint: Edit the three places in docs/setup.md; one sentence each.
pass_cases: 1. docs/setup.md line on project backups names <git dir>/relay-backup/ and "none when git holds the file unchanged: git restore".
2. docs/setup.md keeps "~/.claude/settings.json (timestamped backup)" beside the file (outside git, unchanged behaviour).
3. docs/setup.md says relay setup refuses in a linked worktree and what it prints.
reason: docs/setup.md lines 17, 77-78, 84-85, 131-132 name <git dir>/relay-backup/ and the worktree behaviour (by reading).
findings.summary: docs/setup.md still says the settings backup is beside the file; it now goes under .git/relay-backup or is not made

details: PLAUSIBLE as a cost, CONFIRMED as text. The brief allowed a refusal "if naming it right is not exact"; the fixer says exact
naming is impossible because files and registration would point at the worktree. But the main checkout is known exactly
(git worktree list), and the registration is a single path (projects.toml file = <root>/CLAUDE.local.md), so option A is
buildable. Which one is right is the owner's: A costs about 30 agent minutes and touches detect()/register; B is a message.
evidence: lib/relay_setup.py:636 raise ValueError(f"... Run `relay setup {main}` on the main checkout, then merge that change into this branch")
design-arsenal.md 1.1 row 3: "Edits the main checkout, which arsenal's rule says stays clean."
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Git: "keep the primary checkout on its default branch and clean."
failing_case: The arsenal pilot (design-arsenal.md 1.1: arsenal's main checkout stays clean). `relay setup <arsenal>/.worktrees/x` now
prints "Run `relay setup <arsenal>` on the main checkout, then merge that change into this branch". Following it writes
kit.toml, settings.json, bin/ templates and docs/handover.md into the primary checkout (dirty, on master), and "merge that
change" names no commit. Should (one choice): either setup in a worktree writes the tracked files in the worktree and registers
the project under the main checkout's name and CLAUDE.local.md path, or the refusal points at the path that keeps main clean.
fix_hint: Owner picks A or B; B is a one-line message change.
pass_cases: A (name by main): setup(<tmp>/somewt) writes .claude/kit.toml in somewt, registers [mainproj] with file <tmp>/mainproj/CLAUDE.local.md,
and writes nothing in <tmp>/mainproj except CLAUDE.local.md (untracked, ignored).
B (keep refusal): the message names the command that keeps the main checkout clean, or says plainly that setup writes the main
checkout and must be committed there on a branch.
reason: Option A built: no refusal, project named and registered after the main checkout, main checkout untouched (asserted in the Q1 test).
findings.summary: the refusal tells the owner to run setup on the main checkout, which the owner's Git rule and arsenal's rule keep clean
